Red flag? (new mass, haematuria, arrhythmia, failure to thrive, neurological signs)
Urgent tumour evaluation for new mass or haematuria
HRAS sequencing; echo and ECG; abdominal ultrasound; brain and spine imaging
Does HRAS testing confirm a Costello-associated variant?
Consider Noonan or cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome
Structured tumour surveillance with ultrasound and urinalysis
Cardiac monitoring with echo and ECG; manage arrhythmia
Nasogastric or gastrostomy feeding for failure to thrive
Endocrine care, developmental support and genetic counselling
Life expectancy reduced mainly by cardiac complications and malignancy

rows.parameter: Targeted HRAS sequencing or RASopathy panel

cells.text: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, pulmonary stenosis or arrhythmia

rows.parameter: Abdominal and pelvic ultrasound with urinalysis

cells.text: Chiari I malformation or syringomyelia when indicated
Pitfall: misclassification alters cancer risk counselling
Through clinical genetics; no targeted therapy
Serial abdominal and pelvic ultrasound and urinalysis for rhabdomyosarcoma and neuroblastoma
Echocardiography and ECG for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and atrial tachycardia
Nasogastric or gastrostomy feeding in infancy where needed
Symptomatic Chiari I malformation or syringomyelia
HRAS confirmation; most cases arise de novo

flowcharts.title: Diagnosis and management of inflammatory myopathies

nodes.text: Symmetric proximal weakness or myositis rash
CK, myositis antibody panel, EMG and muscle MRI
CK and EMG myopathic?
Consider PMR, fibromyalgia, neuropathy or myasthenia
Classic DM rash or defining antibody?
Muscle biopsy of affected, not end-stage, muscle
Biopsy shows IBM?
Supportive therapy, swallowing and physiotherapy
Screen lungs, heart, swallowing and cancer
Prednisone 1 mg/kg plus steroid-sparing agent
Severe, ILD or refractory?
IV methylprednisolone, IVIG or rituximab
Taper steroids guided by strength and CK

cells.text: Markedly raised, for example above 2000 U/L
Almost always myopathic; over 10 times normal in IMNM

rows.parameter: Normal or mildly raised CK with distal asymmetric weakness

cells.text: Finger flexor and quadriceps weakness over age 50

rows.parameter: Heliotrope rash plus Gottron papules plus nailfold capillary dilatation

cells.text: Biopsy not usually needed with characteristic skin
DM: Mi-2, TIF1-gamma, MDA5, NXP-2, SAE; IMNM: HMGCR, SRP; ASyS: Jo-1; IBM: cN-1A
Define subtype, cancer and lung risk
Positive in up to 80% of DM and PM
Negative ANA does not exclude myositis
Localise to muscle, show oedema, guide biopsy
Needed in every suspected PM to exclude IBM
Adult DM carries about 15% cancer risk in first 2 to 3 years
Distal asymmetric weakness, older age, steroid-refractory
Biopsy: rimmed vacuoles, p62, COX-negative fibres
Older age, pain and stiffness, high ESR and CRP
Statins, fibrates, niacin, glucocorticoids, zidovudine, colchicine, amiodarone, chloroquine, hydroxychloroquine, d-penicillamine
Improves when drug stopped (unlike anti-HMGCR myopathy)
Weakness with normal CK on high-dose steroids
Family history, chronic course; may show inflammation
Pain and fatigue with normal strength
First line for DM, PM, IMNM, ASyS
About 1 mg/kg daily, maximum 80 mg; taper once strength normalises
Severe disease, dysphagia or respiratory weakness
0.5 to 1 g daily for 3 to 5 days
Start with or soon after steroids
Methotrexate, azathioprine or tacrolimus; prefer non-methotrexate agents with ILD
Dysphagia, respiratory muscle weakness, poor steroid response, anti-HMGCR myopathy
Often effective as monotherapy in anti-HMGCR
Refractory disease or ASyS with ILD
No effective immunotherapy; physiotherapy, occupational and swallowing therapy
Adult DM, especially over 40 or with TIF1-gamma or NXP-2
Age-appropriate screening; CT chest, abdomen, pelvis, ovarian ultrasound, colonoscopy in high risk
Serial CK (normalises in 6 to 12 weeks), bone protection, Pneumocystis prophylaxis, vaccines
